nodes.label: AiProvider interface
nodes.rationale: AiTurn.content is opaque and provider-owned because OpenRouter requires the reasoning block sequence to match the original request unmodified — the same verbatim-replay contract the existing assistantTurn() honours. Consequence: a conversation cannot change provider mid-flight, so provider is resolved once per run and threaded through.

nodes.label: Anthropic adapter
nodes.rationale: Wraps today's code with no behavioural change. The timeout: 600_000 is load-bearing — without it the SDK throws synchronously ('Streaming is required…') for max_tokens implying >10 min and the corrective path would mask it as AI_PLAN_FAILED.

nodes.label: OpenRouter adapter
nodes.rationale: OpenRouter's wire format is OpenAI Chat Completions with no Anthropic /v1/messages passthrough, so pointing the existing SDK's baseURL at it does not work and an adapter is required. Uses Zod 4's native z.toJSONSchema() for response_format, and validates the returned JSON against the same schema so a non-conforming payload degrades to parsed:null and the existing corrective retry.

nodes.label: openrouter-policy (data_collection deny + zdr)
nodes.rationale: Help pages tell customers the brief is not used to train AI models, so routing through third parties has to keep that true in code, not in prose. Hardcoded with no env override; allow_fallbacks:false is not optional because without it routing can escape the allowlist.

nodes.label: Cost precedence: usage.cost over aiRunCostUsd
nodes.rationale: ai-pricing.ts hardcodes per-1M rates and once understated by 33% because a published introductory rate was applied without checking the account. The provider knows what it billed; never guess. Reading billed cost also retires the cache-accounting hazard, since cache reads and writes are already priced into usage.cost. servedModel is stamped from the response rather than the requested constant.

nodes.label: §0 prompt cherry-pick (stable rule IDs H1–H7 / S1–S5)
nodes.rationale: Lands as a separate commit BEFORE any bench arm runs so the prompt is a constant across all arms. Stable rule IDs plus 'cite the rule id that blocked it' make unschedulable reasons machine-classifiable, which the shootout scoring depends on. Rejected: a model-authored verification self-report (the engine referee is deterministic and authoritative, and output tokens are ~90% of run cost) and a needs_clarification status.

nodes.label: Two-stage candidate shootout
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 screens n=1 on the dense teams-15 pack only, because dense is the discriminator (haiku matched sonnet exactly on individuals-50 and produced 20/43/100 warnings on teams-15). The adapter-fidelity control arm runs the same model over a different transport so any divergence is our bug, not the model's — the only way to catch subtle reasoning-replay mismatch, which shows up as degraded repair quality rather than an exception.

nodes.label: Candidate eligibility filter
nodes.rationale: Requires reasoning support (no-thinking left blocking conflicts on 2/3 dense runs AND cost more, because repairs resend prior output as input), structured outputs, a policy-surviving endpoint, and ≥128k context (observed output alone averages 29,858 tokens). The eligible set is committed with the generation date and verbatim filter output so the shootout is reproducible.

nodes.label: ai-fixture-server dual mode
nodes.rationale: Gains an OpenRouter-shaped mode so e2e and smoke cover both paths. Mocked suites cannot catch wire-level traps — the SDK constructor-timeout bug was invisible to every mocked test — so the live bench is the real wire test.

nodes.label: Rejected: OpenRouter presets
nodes.source_location: What OpenRouter is and is not
nodes.rationale: Presets would move model choice out of code, but schedule.ts deliberately stamps the runtime model onto the ledger and the bench sets SCHEDULING_AI_MODEL per arm. A preset makes both record '@preset/foo' and destroys per-model attribution.
